subject: EU edge fallback: temporary degraded throughput — action recommended
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@acme-data.ai>, support@acme-data.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU edge fallback: temporary degraded throughput — action recommended

Hi Samantha —

Quick heads up from Redwood: beginning 07:50 UTC we observed a sustained throughput reduction affecting a subset of requests routed through our EU edge pool servicing Acme's production workload. To preserve availability we automatically routed new sessions to a smaller fallback model variant which increased per-request latency and reduced effective throughput.

What happened (short):
- Trigger: abnormal KV cache evictions on the EU edge cluster followed by cascading scheduling congestion.
- Automatic response: smart-routing policy moved traffic to fallback model variant (cpu/quantized) in EU region to avoid 503s.
- User impact: higher P95 latency (approx +220ms on average) and lower sustained throughput for heavy burst traffic for ~90 minutes.

We posted an incident note on our public status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20261120-eu-edge and are collecting traces.

What we recommend for Acme immediately:
1) If you have capacity, switch long-lived inference sessions to our eu-central dedicated pool (recommended) — Laura can help enable access and provide a temporary burst allocation.
2) For short-term mitigation, update your routing header to prefer eu-west-2 region while we stabilize (we can script this change for you).
3) If you need credits or an SLA exception due to missed latency targets today, loop Ben and I and we’ll expedite.

I’ll follow up with a timeline and a postmortem once we’ve finished root-cause analysis. Attaching a timeline snapshot and the fallback config used.

Thanks and sorry for the disruption — we’ll keep you closely updated.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — edge-fallback-config.txt (text)
From: Samantha Reed <samantha@acme-data.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, support@acme-data.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU edge fallback: temporary degraded throughput — action recommended

Olga —

Thanks for the quick note. We definitely saw an increase in slowness on our side (page alerts). A couple questions:
- ETA for full stabilization / rollback to primary model?
- Can you confirm whether any requests were dropped or only slowed? We need to understand if we missed inference outputs.
- If we accept the suggested region switch, will session affinity break or will we need to restart clients?

We’re on a tight weekend launch so this is visible to several product teams. Please escalate any credit/SLA paths.

— Samantha
Principal ML Engineer, Acme Data & Analytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@acme-data.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, support@acme-data.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU edge fallback: temporary degraded throughput — action recommended

Samantha — thanks, quick answers: 
- Stabilization ETA: engineering estimates initial remediation within 45–60 minutes; full rollback dependent on cache warm-up (~2 hours max). We will push rolling changes to the EU edge and monitor for KV eviction rate.
- Drop vs slowdown: preliminary logs show no 5xx error spikes for Acme’s API key — requests were served from fallback variant (slower) rather than dropped. We will confirm with end-to-end traces.
- Session affinity: switching region will create new sessions; short-lived client connections will reconnect automatically. For long-lived sessions we recommend a controlled restart — we can coordinate a scripted restart window.

Ben and Laura — can you assist with a temporary dedicated allocation and any credit/SLA communications if Acme requests?

I’m standing by to jump on a call with Acme if helpful.

— Olga
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU edge fallback: temporary degraded throughput — action recommended

Adding a note from pricing/ops:
- I’ll provision a temporary dedicated burst pool in eu-central for Acme for the next 72 hours; will confirm allocation ID in ~15 minutes.
- If Acme requests credits for the period where observed latency exceeded their SLA, we can offer a service credit equal to one day of hosted usage or an account-level credit scaled to measured impact — I’ll await their request details.

Laura — can you own the technical enablement and the quick-turn quota change? Olga — loop me into any customer calls.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@acme-data.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, support@acme-data.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU edge fallback: temporary degraded throughput — action recommended

Hi Samantha / team —

We’ve completed the immediate remediation: edge scheduling knobs were adjusted and KV eviction rate has dropped to baseline. Rolling rollback to primary model has started; we expect sessions to use the primary variant within the next ~30–45 minutes as caches warm. No dropped requests were found in the customer traces we’ve verified.

Practical next steps for Acme (what we can do for you):
- I will open a maintenance window to help you restart any long-lived clients, script available here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/postmortem-INC-20261120
- Ben has provisioned a temporary eu-central burst pool (alloc-ACME-11-20) for 72 hours.
- We’ll share a full postmortem by Tuesday that includes timeline, root cause, and remediation plan.

We’ll keep the status page updated and I’ll set up a short sync with the Acme infra squad if you want a walk-through.

Thanks for your patience — Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Cloud Operations, Redwood Inference
